subject: general
question: India borrowed the DPSP from the ______ Constitution.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Irish.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DPSP** stands for **Directive Principles of State Policy, **which are guidelines for the government to ensure** social and economic justice **in India.
 
• The Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of DPSP from the** Irish Constitution,** which had similar provisions.
 
• The Irish Constitution's DPSP was influenced by the **Catholic social teachings** and the **ideas of social justice.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Australian Constitution** has no DPSP, but it has provisions related to the** division of powers** between the federal and state governments.

 
 
• The Australian Constitution is the** country's highest law.**
 
• The six autonomous British colonies in Australia—**New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria, and Western Australia**—conducted a series of conventions between **1891 and 1898** to draft the Constitution. 
 
 
 
• The** German Constitution** has a similar concept called** Grundgesetz, **which includes** fundamental rights and principles** for the state's welfare.
 
• Approved in Bonn on **May 8, 1949, **the West German Constitution went into force on** May 23**, following its approval on** May 12** by the occupying **western Allies of World War II.**
